title: CRM Migration Checklist: Move Customer Data Without Losing Context
description: A step-by-step CRM migration checklist covering discovery, data cleanup, field mapping, integration testing, permissions, cutover, rollback, and post-launch reconciliation.
author: PilotStack Editorial Team

sections.title: Set Scope and Ownership
sections.body: Name one migration owner and representatives for sales, marketing, support, data, and security. Document which records will move, which will be archived, and which historical details must remain searchable. Agree on a cutover date, a freeze window for schema changes, and the business workflows that cannot be interrupted. Define acceptance criteria before work begins—for example, required record types migrate, key relationships remain intact, integrations pass tests, and users can complete a standard customer workflow. Make unresolved decisions visible with an owner and deadline.

sections.title: Inventory the Source System
sections.body: Export or inspect the current schema, record counts, custom fields, picklists, attachments, notes, activity history, automations, and integrations. Identify fields nobody uses, duplicate representations of the same information, and undocumented formulas. Record the source of truth for each important value. Take a protected backup and verify that it can be restored or read independently of the old CRM. Do not start transforming data until the team knows which records are authoritative and which are stale, duplicated, or legally required to be retained.

sections.title: Clean and Map the Data
sections.body: Create a field mapping document that describes source, destination, transformation, validation, and owner for each field.
items: Normalize dates, phone numbers, country codes, and picklist values.
Define duplicate matching rules for contacts and accounts, including shared email addresses.
Map owners, teams, lifecycle stages, and opportunity stages explicitly.
Decide how blank values differ from unknown, not applicable, or intentionally removed values.
Preserve source IDs in a migration reference field where they are needed for reconciliation.
Record fields that will not migrate and explain where the historical information remains available.

sections.title: Run a Small Trial Migration
sections.body: Use a representative sample that includes ordinary records, duplicates, long histories, attachments, inactive customers, and edge cases. Import it into a non-production environment if available. Check record counts and compare a sample field by field against the source. Test relationships between accounts, contacts, opportunities, notes, and activities. Ask users to complete real tasks using the migrated data. Fix mapping errors and repeat the trial until the acceptance criteria are met; a successful import job alone does not prove that the information is complete or usable.

sections.title: Rebuild Integrations and Permissions
sections.body: Document every system that reads or writes CRM data and test each connection independently. Verify field mapping, sync direction, retry behavior, rate limits, duplicate-event handling, and error alerts. Recreate roles and permissions using least privilege rather than copying broad access from the old system by default. Test as a standard user, manager, administrator, and any guest or service account. Rotate credentials where necessary and confirm that logs do not expose sensitive customer information.

sections.title: Plan Cutover and Rollback
sections.body: Write a cutover runbook with the order of operations, responsible people, communication plan, data freeze, final export, import, reconciliation, integration switch, and go/no-go decision. Define objective rollback triggers, such as missing critical records, broken sales workflows, or an integration failure that cannot be resolved within the agreed window. Keep the old system available in read-only mode until the new CRM is accepted and retention requirements are satisfied. Do not delete the source data immediately after the first successful login.

sections.title: Reconcile and Sign Off
sections.body: Compare source and destination counts by object type and important status, then inspect samples across each critical workflow. Investigate missing records, changed owners, lost relationships, duplicate creation, invalid dates, and mismatched totals. Reconcile high-value business records separately instead of relying only on aggregate counts. Record accepted exceptions and obtain sign-off from the owners of sales, marketing, support, and security. Keep evidence of the reconciliation so later reporting differences can be traced to the migration.

sections.title: Support the First 30 Days
sections.body: Provide short role-specific training, a place to report issues, and a daily review of migration defects during the initial period. Track errors, adoption friction, duplicate rates, integration failures, and the completion of key workflows. Prioritize issues that block customer follow-up or corrupt trusted data. Review permissions and remove temporary migration access. Once the system stabilizes, archive the runbook, mapping, scripts, and decisions so the next system change can reuse the lessons without repeating the same risks.
